newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sanofi profit up, beauty out of the red.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi profit up, beauty out of the red.

text.p: French health and beauty products company Sanofi SA on Tuesday said its 1996 net earnings increased by 11 percent to 1.743 billion francs ($308 million), with beauty products back in the black after a first half loss.

The company, in which Elf-Aquitaine has a 38 percent stake, said the year was marked by relative stability of the French franc in comparison with other major world currencies, with the exception of the Japanese yen.
Sanofi sales were up three percent to 23.645 billion and earnings per share rose eight percent to 16.80. ($ = 5.658 French Francs)
Analysts had been expecting an average earnings per share figure of 17.3 francs, according to Edinburg Financial Publishing, and 17.1 francs according to Jacques Chahine Finance in Paris.
Sanofi said there had been very weak economic growth in Europe, with the exception of the U.K., which increased competition.
In the health segment, operating profit rose 5.5 percent to 3.696 billion francs after taking in account higher research and development spending.
In the beauty segment, Sanofi said the European market for the selective distribution of luxury goods was adversely impacted by general sluggish consumption in Europe.

But after a 74 million loss in the first half, operating profit for the second half was close to that of the 1995 period and in the full year the operating profit was 236 million francs, against 331 million in 1995.

Yves Rocher posted growth in both sales and net earnings while Nina Ricci reported a decline in sales and earnings due to the difficulties experienced by the distinctive fragrance industry as a whole, Sanofi said.
